title: Compass notes — 90-day evidence clipboard
content:
Purpose and use
- Quick personal clipboard for the next 1:1 and calibration. Not polished — copy snippets to the manager email or performance doc.
- Goal: have 6–8 short, concrete evidence points mapped to behaviors and impact by the time I prep the deck.

Topline narrative (one-liner)
- Shifted hiring funnel hygiene and interview calibration in Q1 to reduce time-to-hire for IC2 roles by ~18% (measured baseline → current; see metric below). Focused on interviewer enablement + scorecard clarity.

Evidence snippets (raw/unfiltered, paste-ready)
- "Led 3 interviewer calibration sessions (Feb 2, Feb 16, Mar 2) — standardized rubrics; observed drop in score variance from 1.6 to 0.9 across panelists for backend IC2."
- "Created interview guide v2 and distributed to 24 interviewers; >85% reported higher confidence in post-session survey (n=18 responses)."
- "Partnered with Talent Ops to triage backlog of 46 open requisitions; re-prioritized 12 roles and reduced backlog by 30% in 4 weeks."
- "Quick experiment: introduced 15-min phone screens for top-tier candidates, cut scheduling churn by ~22% (tracked Feb 8–Mar 1)."
- "Ad-hoc stakeholder: supported Eng PM on intake process; helped define acceptance criteria so 2 hiring managers could close offers with clearer expectations."

Metrics to cite (show the math)
- time-to-offer (IC2 backend): baseline 28d → current 23d = -18% (data from hiring dashboard, pipeline filtered by role tag 'backend-ic2').
- interview panel variance: baseline s=1.6 → current s=0.9 (panel score SD across 24 interviews).
- backlog reduction: 46 → 32 open reqs in 28 days.
- candidate no-show for scheduling: 11% → 8.6% during trial window (Feb 8–Mar 1).

How this ties to org priorities (line by line)
- Ops reliability: fewer open roles = more predictable capacity planning for Q2 launches.
- Hiring velocity: faster time-to-offer reduces recruiter churn and cost-per-hire.
- Manager experience: clearer scorecards reduce ramp friction for new ICs (less rework in first 90 days).

Micro-behaviors and examples (for manager Qs)
- Ownership: "Picked up backlog triage and pushed initial prioritization within 48 hours — documented rationale and follow-ups."
- Collaboration: "Paired with Talent and Eng leads to get commitments on interviewers for next cycle."
- Clarity: "Reduced interview guide length by 40% and annotated with sample answers so panelists spend less time guessing."

5-week focus experiment (concrete plan + check-ins)
- Week 0 (now): finalize scorecard changes and push guide comms. Slack channel #hiring-hygiene — pin guide + 1-pager.
- Week 1–2: run two calibration sessions (one recorded); collect quick pulse survey.
- Week 3: run pilot with 10 interviews using the new phone screen template; measure scheduling churn and panel variance.
- Week 4–5: iterate on guide; create one-slide summary for leadership sync. 
- Success signals: variance <1.1, time-to-offer trending down, positive manager feedback (>= 4/5).

Manager prep TL;DR (what I want to say in 1:1)
- Quick stat: "Time-to-offer for backend IC2 improved by ~18% since Feb initiatives."
- Ask: "Thumbs up to roll phone-screen template org-wide for IC2? If yes, I'll coordinate ops and comms."
- Ask (people): "Need 6 interviewers released for the calibration program over the next 8 weeks (2 per team)."
- Risks: "If we scale without calibration, we'll reintroduce score variance — I propose gating scale on panel training completion."

Unresolved / questions to raise
- Do we want to include hiring scorecard changes as part of the formal onboarding checklist for new managers? (pro: consistency; con: possible friction)
- Should interviewer training be optional or required for hiring managers requesting >3 hires in a quarter?

Notes to self (short prompts)
- Bring analyst dashboard screenshot to 1:1.
- Update confluence page with 'last updated' timestamp after Week 2 exercise.
- Draft manager note for comms (<= 150 words) and send for review by Wed.

Snippets for the manager email (pick one)
- Option A (concise): "Quick update: reduced backend IC2 time-to-offer ~18% after hygiene changes. Proposal: standardize phone-screen template for IC2 roles to keep momentum. Can we roll this org-wide?"
- Option B (context): "Over the last 6 weeks I ran calibration sessions, pilot phone screens, and a backlog triage. Early indicators: lower panel variance and improved scheduling. Recommend a controlled roll-out and asking for 6 interviewers for continued calibration."

Archive cues (where to copy each item)
- Metrics + screenshot: copy to /confluence/hiring-ops/metrics (linked artifact)
- Calibration notes + recording: add to candidate-experience page
- Manager email: paste into performance prep doc under 'manager-comm'

Quick log (timestamps for later reference)
- Feb 2: calibration session (notes: session-20260202.md)
- Feb 8: launched phone screen pilot tracker (sheet id: hires-feb-pilot)
- Feb 16: follow-up calibration, updated guide v1.1
- Mar 2: recorded calibration + final edits to guide

Done-list (satisfying the checklist)
- [x] guide v2 created and shared with 24 interviewers
- [x] initial calibration run + recording
- [ ] pilot complete and metrics validated (due Mar 8)
- [ ] manager email drafted and sent

Reflection prompts (for end-of-90-day write-up)
- What decisions did I influence and how did I document them?
- Which experiments failed quickly and what did we learn?
- Where did I need more stakeholder influence and how could I have done that earlier?

Random scratch lines (for mental model)
- "Less is more" — shorter guides increase panel adherence.
- If we can prove variance reduction, operational leaders sign-off is easier.

End.
